messages:
marta: quick heads-up, ran hybrid quant bring-up for orion-14b on convo+summarize slices. results are a bit odd — int6 latency improved but quality hit varies by slice.

kevin: can you drop the short numbers?

priya: baseline: fp16 for our current prod orion-14b. bench summary below.

bench-bot: ```
# bench run: bench --model orion-14b --seq 1024 --batch 2
fp16: p50=210ms p95=420ms toks/sec=34 cost_per_1k=$0.45
int8: p50=170ms p95=360ms toks/sec=48 cost_per_1k=$0.33
int6: p50=140ms p95=540ms toks/sec=60 cost_per_1k=$0.24
# eval (slices)
# multi-turn summarize (n=800): fp16=45.2 BLEU-like=0.68 halluc=2.1%
int8=43.6 BLEU-like=0.64 halluc=5.8%
int6=40.0 BLEU-like=0.57 halluc=10.2%
# chit-chat (n=500): fp16 accept=92% int8 accept=90% int6 accept=89%
# short QA (n=400): fp16 acc=81% int8 acc=78% int6 acc=75%
```

sloh: that halluc rate on summarize for int8 is concerning. product will hate 3-4% delta.

marta: initial thought: route summarization to fp16, keep conversation/chat on int8 to save cost. int6 only for internal background indexing.

kevin: rough econ if 50% chat->int8, 30% summarize->fp16, 20% background->int6: cost_per_1k = 0.5*0.33 + 0.3*0.45 + 0.2*0.24 = $0.336 -> ~25% saving vs all fp16 ($0.45).

priya: can we reduce halluc without sacrificing int8 econ? maybe selective prompt engineering or adding small decoding constraints.

marta: tried top-p tuning, reduced halluc by ~0.8pp but token output reduced slightly, net cost neutral. still not within product tolerance.

sloh: propose conservative rollout: canary 5% int8 for chat, shadow-summarize to fp16 and compare. set alerts for halluc + support tickets.

kevin: also add token inflation metric; int6 saw +4% tokens in some transcripts which changes cost model.

priya: ok i'll assemble the slice definitions and the canary YAML. tagging bench-bot to export full CSVs and eval artifacts.

marta: thanks folks. i'll draft the PR with routing rules and the econ calc.

bench-bot: attaching artifacts: /artifacts/orion14b/bringup/20250201/*
